title: company-command-post-retro-and-risk-brief
summary: This all-hands focused on a retro of Q3 operational incidents, an update on risk posture and mitigation steps, a short-term hiring pause and prioritization, and readiness for an upcoming compliance audit. Leadership shared concrete actions and owners; there was Q&A around customer SLAs, dedicated vs hosted roadmaps, and how the changes affect teams and hiring. Tone: candid, pragmatic, emphasis on mission continuity and targeted cost/time tradeoffs.
action_items: Jonah Kim - produce incident timeline and remediation checklist - due 2026-09-07
Priya Agarwal - reprioritize roadmap to focus on SLA hardening and telemetry - due 2026-09-10
Mateo Ruiz - run scale bench for EU region and share results - due 2026-09-14
Sara Li - finalize headcount freeze exceptions process and communicate to managers - due 2026-09-04
Claire Bennett - send follow-up note with runway and budget context to all staff - due 2026-09-02
next_steps: Leadership to post the incident postmortem doc and run dev/ops office hours
Teams to consolidate non-critical roadmap items into backlog for Q4 planning
Compliance team to publish SOC2/ISO audit checklist and required artifact owners
People team to host an AMA on hiring freeze and exception criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Claire (CEO): hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, um we're gonna kick off the.. the command post retro. keeping this tight, plan is 60 minutes. i know it sounds heavy but - important.
[00:18] Claire (CEO): quick housekeeping: recording's on, q's in the slack channel or use raise-hand, we'll try to take live.
[00:30] Mateo (CTO): morning all, Mateo here. first slide is operational scorecards, and then incident review.
[00:38] Claire (CEO): okay, priya you're on product update after mateo.
[00:42] Priya (VP Product): cheers.
[00:45] [00:52] Mateo (CTO): so, the big thing this quarter was the cascading memory leak in the KV cache allocator that hit hosted-prod on 2026-08-22. the leak started during a high-traffic model rollout, there were multiple throttles and then we had to failover to standby in us-west-2.
[01:12] Jonah (Head Engineering): yep, and to add, the fallback logic didn't cutover cleanly because the routing policies were using an older model tag, so there was a version mismatch that caused elevated latencies during the failover window.
[01:28] Claire (CEO): rough. What was the customer impact?
[01:32] Mateo (CTO): about 1.8% of requests saw >5s tail latency for roughly three hours, and we had 24 enterprise customers on reserved capacity who saw increased error rates for a short period. we opened pager cycles and eventually throttled new requests while we flushed the KV caches.
[01:50] [02:00] Audience (multiple): uh-huh, mm.
[02:05] Jonah (Head Engineering): root cause: a concurrent GC path that didn't free some pinned pages, exacerbated by a recent micro-optimization in the serving runtime. that optimization was shipped as part of a perf patch two weeks prior.
[02:26] Priya (VP Product): product angle - we pushed a model variant and the traffic shape changed (longer context windows) which stressed the path. insufficent regression coverage for long-context cases, so lesson there.
[02:45] Claire (CEO): i want a short postmortem doc by monday, with remediation, blameless tone. jonah?
[02:51] Jonah (Head Engineering): yes, i'll own that.
[02:55] [03:05] Mateo (CTO): mitigation already done: revert micro-opt, add guardrails in runtime, and an auto-eviction threshold for KV cache. but we need better canarying and longer tail-testing.
[03:20] Claire (CEO): okay good. second big topic: runway and hiring. i know folks are anxious. sara?
[03:29] Sara (VP People): yes. short version: we are instituting a temporary hiring pause for non-critical roles effective immediately. exceptions for revenue-critical, security, and legal functions will be evaluated case-by-case. managers, you will get a template to request exceptions.
[03:47] Audience: silence, murmur.
[03:50] Claire (CEO): why now? can you give the numbers?
[03:55] Sara (VP People): we've got 9 months of runway under current spend growth assumptions; with forecasted deals pushing, that's healthy but tight. this pause is a conservative step to maintain runway if macro slows.
[04:10] Claire (CEO): it's a pause, not a hiring freeze forever. we'll be deliberate, prioritize mission-critical hires.
[04:16] [04:28] Priya (VP Product): on roadmap reprioritization: we're pulling forward SLA hardening, telemetry, and rollout safety features. lower-priority UX polish and exploratory integrations will be deferred. we'll share the reprioritized list by next week.
[04:47] Mateo (CTO): also re: regional capacity planning - EU region capacity needs more investment; we've seen growth in EMEA and need to make sure latency SLOs are met. i'm proposing a short burst of reserved capacity in frankfurt while we run a collector bench.
[05:05] Claire (CEO): any cost estimate?
[05:08] Mateo (CTO): ballpark $210k for the burst for 3 months, plus one-time infra setup. it's cheaper than emergency hot-standby migrations.
[05:19] Claire (CEO): okay we'll include that in the budget reforecast.
[05:24] [05:30] Audience question (Slack): what does this mean for hiring in eng?
[05:34] Sara (VP People): engineers: critical platform and infra roles remain eligible. everything else paused. we know it's disruptive; we'll do manager AMAs.
[05:42] Jonah (Head Engineering): to be explicit - if you're on a product that directly impacts platform SLOs or revenue-critical tracks, we will still hire.
[05:50] Claire (CEO): next topic: compliance audit. priya? (sorry mateo?)
[05:57] Priya (VP Product): compliance update - we have a SOC2 readiness audit scheduled for 2026-10-13. security team will need owners to sign off on evidence, and infra teams to freeze major infra changes a week before audits.
[06:16] Mateo (CTO): the audit will check encryption-at-rest keys (kms) rotation logs, RBAC artifacts, and retention policies. we need to ensure the private deployment docs for on-prem customers are up to date.
[06:30] Claire (CEO): anything high risk?
[06:33] Mateo (CTO): a couple of control gaps: automated key rotation evidence gaps and some missing runbooks for backup restores. low-medium risk but fixable fast.
[06:46] [07:00] Priya (VP Product): product will own on-prem docs updates, compliance team will post checklist.
[07:06] Claire (CEO): next: risk register and mitigation priorities. i want top three risks we can fix in 30 days.
[07:15] Mateo (CTO): 1) KV cache regression / runtime stability - fix in 7-14 days.
[07:21] Mateo (CTO): 2) telemetry blind spots for tail latency - 14-21 days.
[07:27] Mateo (CTO): 3) audit evidence and runbooks - 21-30 days.
[07:32] Claire (CEO): good. shoutouts before Q&A?
[07:36] Sara (VP People): shoutout to infra on-call (team redwood-ops) for 26-hour ops rotation, and to the product triage squad for rapid rollback.
[07:47] Audience applause.
[07:52] [08:05] Q&A segment starts. Claire: we'll take questions from slack first.
[08:12] Slack Q: will dedicated customers see pricing changes?
[08:16] Claire (CEO): no immediate price changes. pricing reviews are part of later planning, but we won't do surprise increases. dedicated contracts remain honored.
[08:25] Slack Q: are there layoffs planned?
[08:28] Claire (CEO): no layoffs planned currently. pause on hiring != layoffs. we are optimizing spend and prioritizing.
[08:36] Audience: sighs, relieved.
[08:40] Live Q from engineering: what's the long-term approach to KV cache?
[08:44] Mateo (CTO): long-term: rearchitect to a sharded, quota-aware cache with better eviction semantics and observable metrics. short-term: eviction threshold and guarded allocation.
[08:57] [09:10] Jonah (Head Engineering): also adding more canary traffic profiles that include long-context sessions, and we'll extend the canary window to 48 hours for critical runtime changes.
[09:22] Claire (CEO): how does this change our release cadence?
[09:25] Priya (VP Product): slower on infra-impacting patches, more staged rollouts. feature teams can still do daily deploys if they don't touch runtime kernels.
[09:37] [09:50] Slack Q: what about customers in APAC?
[09:53] Mateo (CTO): APAC growth continues; we have a plan to run local egress and caching in sydney region next quarter depending on capacity outcomes.
[10:03] Claire (CEO): okay, wrap with commitments. claire: i'll send financial context note by tomorrow, sara will do manager guidance on exceptions, jonah will post incident timeline, priya will reprioritize roadmap.
[10:20] Jonah (Head Engineering): one more technical note: there was some mislabelling in our routing table that caused the failover to look like a model mismatch, it's partially a process gap in deployment prep. we'll add an automated routing-table validator to the CI.
[10:37] Audience: mm.
[10:41] [10:50] Priya (VP Product): also, product will run a week-long "safety sprint" where teams can chip away at rollout safety features. details in the retrospective doc.
[10:58] Claire (CEO): last thing - culture. this is a stressful moment; recognition matters. we'll pause non-essential all-hands social spend and instead invest in targeted team support (meals, mental health credits). sara, over to you.
[11:15] Sara (VP People): yes, people-first: managers get a playbook for 1:1s, and we'll hold optional office hours. also reminder: the anonymous pulse is open for feedback.
[11:30] Claire (CEO): thanks everyone. closing notes: be transparent with customers, keep the mission focus. we'll do a follow-up next week.
[11:40] Audience (multiple): thanks, bye.
